Package edu.cnu.mdi.sim.ga.triimage

Class ImageApproximationProblem

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.sim.ga.triimage.ImageApproximationProblem
All Implemented Interfaces:
GAProblem<PolygonChromosome>
public final class ImageApproximationProblem extends Object implements GAProblem<PolygonChromosome>
A GAProblem that evolves a population of PolygonChromosome instances to approximate a target image using semi-transparent triangles.

Fitness

Fitness is the negated mean squared error (MSE) between the rendered chromosome and the target image, computed channel-wise over the RGB channels: 

   fitness = −MSE
   MSE     = Σ [(ΔR² + ΔG² + ΔB²) / 255²] / (pixels × 3)

Following the GA convention of higher = better, a perfect match has fitness 0.0 and a maximally wrong solution has fitness -1.0. The alpha channel is excluded from the error metric — it affects appearance through blending but is not directly penalized.

Performance

Three optimizations keep fitness evaluation fast enough for interactive population sizes (≥ 100 individuals):

  1. Reduced fitness resolution. The target image is pre-scaled to FITNESS_W × FITNESS_H pixels at construction. All fitness evaluations render at this small size. The view calls PolygonChromosome.render(int, int) at full display resolution independently. Typical speedup: 6–10× over full-resolution evaluation.
  2. Thread-local render buffers. The BufferedImage and pixel array used during each fitness() call are allocated once per thread and reused for every subsequent call on that thread. This eliminates per-evaluation heap allocation and GC pressure. The buffers are stored in ThreadLocal fields so the design is also safe for future parallel evaluation (see GAConfig.parallelEvaluation). Typical speedup: 2–3× over per-call allocation.
  3. Integer MSE accumulation. The inner pixel loop accumulates squared channel differences as long integers and divides by 255² exactly once after the loop, avoiding per-pixel floating-point division. Typical speedup: 1.1–1.2×.

Usage


 BufferedImage target = ImageIO.read(new File("mona_lisa.png"));
 GAProblem<PolygonChromosome> problem = new ImageApproximationProblem(target, 50);

 GAOperators<PolygonChromosome> ops = new GAOperators<>(new TournamentSelection<>(5), new UniformBlendCrossover(),
 		new GaussianMutation(0.05), new ElitistReplacement<>(2));

 GeneticAlgorithmSimulation<PolygonChromosome> sim = new GeneticAlgorithmSimulation<>(problem, GAConfig.defaults(),
 		ops);

  • Field Details

    • FITNESS_W

      public static final int FITNESS_W
      Width in pixels used for fitness evaluation rendering.

      Reducing this value increases evaluation speed at the cost of a coarser fitness signal. Values in the range 60–100 work well for triangle counts up to ~100. The view always renders at the original image dimensions via PolygonChromosome.render(int, int).

  • Constructor Details

    • ImageApproximationProblem

      public ImageApproximationProblem(BufferedImage target, int numTriangles)
      Construct an image approximation problem for the given target image and triangle count.

      The target image is immediately scaled to FITNESS_W × FITNESS_H using bilinear interpolation and its pixel data is extracted into an int[] array. This pre-processing is done once at construction so that fitness(edu.cnu.mdi.sim.ga.triimage.PolygonChromosome) can operate purely on primitive arrays without touching the original image.

      Parameters:
      target - the image to approximate (non-null; any dimensions)
      numTriangles - number of triangles per chromosome (must be > 0)
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if target is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if numTriangles is not positive

  • Method Details

    • fitness

      public double fitness(PolygonChromosome c)
      Compute the fitness of a chromosome as the negated mean squared error between its rendered image and the target.

      The chromosome is rendered into a thread-local BufferedImage at FITNESS_W × FITNESS_H pixels. Pixel differences are accumulated as integer squared errors (Fix 3) and normalized to [0, 1] after the loop. The result is negated so that higher fitness corresponds to a closer match.

      Fitness values lie in [-1, 0]:

      • 0.0 — perfect match
      • -1.0 — maximally wrong (every channel maximally wrong)

      This method is safe to call from multiple threads simultaneously because it uses only ThreadLocal buffers and reads immutable fields.

      Specified by:
      fitness in interface GAProblem<PolygonChromosome>
      Parameters:
      c - the chromosome to evaluate (non-null)
      Returns:
      fitness in [-1, 0], higher is better

    • initialPopulation

      public GAPopulation<PolygonChromosome> initialPopulation(int size, Random rng)
      Generate an initial population of size randomly initialized chromosomes.

      Each individual is produced by randomIndividual(Random) independently. The returned population is a SimpleGAPopulation backed by a fresh ArrayList.
